properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued November 17 at 1:43PM EST until November 17 at 2:00PM EST by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
For the following areas...
Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 nm west of Dry Tortugas
out 60 nm...
Gulf of America including Dry Tortugas and Rebecca Shoal Channel...

At 143 PM EST, a possible waterspout was located 13 nm southwest of
Tortugas Ecological Reserve South, moving east at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and large
hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.
Large hail could result in injury and damage to boats.

Locations in the warning include...
Tortugas Ecological Reserve South.
properties.instruction:
Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous
seas. Seek safe harbor immediately.
properties.area: Gulf of America including Dry Tortugas and Rebecca Shoal Channel; Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 NM west of Dry Tortugas out 20 NM; Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 NM west of Dry Tortugas 20 to 60 NM out

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 17 at 2:39PM AST until November 17 at 5:45PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northern Cabo Rojo...
Hormigueros...
Mayaguez...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Overflowing
poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 238 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
properties.area: Cabo Rojo, PR; Hormigueros, PR; Mayaguez, PR

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 17 at 11:13AM MST until November 17 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall.

* WHERE...Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in creeks and normally dry washes is
imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1110 AM MST, Moderate to briefly heavy rain was falling
through the I-17 corridor and Oak Creek Canyon. Minor flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Turkey Creek, Rattlesnake Canyon, Jacks Canyon, Howard Draw,
Walnut Creek, Spring Creek, San Francisco Wash, JD Dam Wash, Tule
Tank Wash, Dry Creek, Coffee Creek, Sycamore Creek, Rarick
Canyon, Oak Creek, Pumphouse Wash, Schultz Creek, Volunteer Wash,
West Fork Oak Creek, Schoolhouse Draw, Dry Beaver Creek and
Sinclair Wash.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sedona, East Flagstaff, Village of Oak Creek, Downtown Flagstaff,
Kachina Village, Munds Park, Forest Highlands, Mountainaire,
Indian Gardens, Pine Flats, Fernow Cabin, Camp Navajo, Northern
Arizona University, Country Club and Sunnyside.
- This includes the following highways...
Interstate 40 between mile markers 187 and 205. Interstate 17
between mile markers 306 and 339. State Route 179 between mile
markers 304 and 313. U.S. Highway 89 near mile marker 419. Route
66 between mile markers 192 and 204. State Route 89A between mile
markers 366 and 398. Highway 180 between mile markers 217 and
218.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Manzanita Campground, Pine Flat Campground, Canyon Vista
Campground, Cave Springs Campground, Canyon Vista Campground,
Taylor Cabin Line Camp, Woody Mountain Campground, Fort Tuthill
Campground, Ponderosa Trails Park, Thorpe Park, Wheeler Park,
Foxglenn Park, Buffalo Park, McPherson Park, Bushmaster Park,
Picture Canyon Preserve and Fort Tuthill County Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Pumphouse Wash, Slide Rock, Encinoso, Grasshopper Point, Midgely
Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing" and Crescent Moon Ranch.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:27AM CST until November 18 at 7:36PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CST Tuesday the stage was 15.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tonight and continue falling to 11.0 feet by Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 9:23AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall over recent weeks has caused river levels on the St.
Johns near Geneva Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage.
River levels are expected slowly rise into this weekend through
Moderate Flood Stage due to additional heavy rainfall over the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 9.3 feet, Many secondary roads are flooded near Lake
Harney. Flooding in the Hatbill Road area near Loughman Lake.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 9.0 to 9.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 9:21AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to continue to remain steady with slight deviations
in river levels through mid to late week due to additional forecast
heavy rainfall.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM EST Tuesday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.1 to 17.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 9:19AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast through at least midweek due to a combination of
northerly winds and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north
through the basin. Rises to Moderate Flood Stage are forecast later
in the week due to the additional heavy rainfall expected.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor to Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.4 feet Sunday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.
